last_action: CUT iOS PREVIEW BUILD 4bc720fe FROM 687ce5b (main), REPLACING 55b80f8a TWO DAYS BEFORE IT EXPIRED. Ad-hoc internal distribution, 5 minutes, no interactive credential setup — the provisioning profile from the dev build still covers the registered iPhone and runs to June 2027. Install by opening the build page ON THE PHONE, not the .ipa: https://expo.dev/accounts/wheredidfranciscogo/projects/juniper/builds/4bc720fe-fe92-43e4-be66-01299573ba12 Fingerprint 3dccf87f is identical to all three earlier previews, which is the check that the native config did not drift. Product-wise this is the same app as 55b80f8a — everything merged since (PRs #2-#6) is dependency overrides, tests and docs, none of which reach the bundle. ALSO REPOINTED THE DOCS: twelve references across STATUS.md, TASKS.md, PLAN.md and this file still named the expiring build, which would have recreated exactly the stale-claim problem this run started with. EARLIER IN THE SAME RUN: PR #6 opened — the "changing the time reschedules" test asserted only that the preference was written, never that anything was rescheduled, so it did not test its own name. The blocker was a flat getItem stub: syncReminders re-reads the pref to rebuild the queue, so the stub handed it the old 09:00 forever and the new time was unobservable no matter what was asserted. Seeded through the stateful mock instead, added the 1-plant guard, and asserted a trigger at the new hour. Verified by mutation rather than by watching it pass: removing the syncReminders call and rebuilding at a hardcoded stale 09:00 both fail the new test, and the SECOND ONE PASSED the old test — the app could have rescheduled every reminder to the wrong time of day and the suite stayed green.
next_action: THE BUILD IS NO LONGER THE BLOCKER; USING IT IS. (1) INSTALL 4bc720fe ON THE PHONE — it expires 2026-09-23 and re-cutting it is a recurring cost until the app is actually lived with, not a task that closes. (2) Move the real garden in: remove the seeded example, add your own plants with photographs, then EXPORT THE DATA — on-device storage means an afternoon of typing has exactly one copy until you make a second. (3) THE WATERING REMINDER HAS STILL NEVER FIRED ON REAL HARDWARE — turn reminders on, pick the next slot ahead of the current hour, leave the phone alone. This is the one thing standing between Phase 1 and done. (4) Two items needing eyes rather than code: whether "Water Marcel" still reads off-centre, and whether the Today footer should report state ("you’re caught up") rather than count plants. (5) Then: Maestro against the device, TestFlight, Play internal. (6) Merge PR #6 when convenient — test-only, does not affect the build.

blockers.description: The watering reminder — the feature the whole app exists for — has never fired on real hardware. Everything around it is tested; delivery itself is not. Build 4bc720fe makes it observable.

iOS preview build 4bc720fe expires 2026-09-23. Ad-hoc internal builds run on a 14-day clock, so an installable copy of Juniper exists only while someone keeps re-cutting one. This stops being a recurring chore only when the app has been lived with and the reminder has been seen to fire.
